text:
anya: Quick thread — we need final alignment on GA commitments before I escalate to PM review. Top open items I see: SLA and credit calc, canary window & rollout policy, pricing tier mapping, API docs + quickstart, support training checklist, telemetry retention, and legal risk language. Who can take which?

ravi: I can take the pricing tier mapping and credit calc. Need the SLA numbers confirmed first though.

paul: Ill own the canary and rollout policy. Proposal: 2-week canary with 3 escalating rings (internal, beta partners, public) + automatic rollback on sustained error-burn > 2% over 30m.

liz: Ill do API docs + quickstart. Will add a "what to expect" section for rate limits and streaming behavior. Need a sample app from eng to include code snippets.

mika: Support training and playbook owner here. Will draft L1/L2 scripts and a 1-hr training deck for CS.

anya: Great. Two quick clarifications: (A) SLA math: do we do monthly uptime-style credits or per-incident credits? (B) Telemetry retention: Ops prefers 14 days by default but we need to call out 90-day for forensic on paid tiers.

ravi: Commercial prefers monthly uptime credits (easier to sell). I'll draft the calc: credit = min(100%, (1 - (monthly downtime / SLA_window)) * 100) with a cap of 50% rebate. Will post example table.

legal-bot: Note: legal requires explicit exclusion for third-party model regressions and force majeure in GA contract. Also want a simple SLA disclaimer for GA that were piloting availability commitments.

paul: Canary detail: add rolling percentage ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48h between rings, with manual gate if error budget burned in previous ring. I'll write the PR for the rollout doc.

liz: For docs example app I'll need a small hosted sample key and model endpoint. Eng, can someone provide a minimal demo token and a short-lived endpoint?

mika: Training checklists: include escalation matrix, sample pager messages, and canned customer responses. Also plan a 1-week shadow period post-GA where CS sits with eng-oncall for knowledge transfer.

ops-bot: telemetry-cost: estimate: 14-day retention = $3.1k/mo per 100k requests; 90-day = $7.4k/mo per 100k requests (approx). Contact @paul for per-model breakdown.

anya: Good catch on shadow week. Let's make that optional for self-serve customers but mandatory for Dedicated/Enterprise. Also, mark Enterprise as separate procurement path (not GA).

ravi: Pricing tiers proposal: Free dev tier (best-effort, no SLA), Standard (14-day telemetry, SLA credits up to 30%), Dedicated (reserved capacity, 90-day telemetry, commercial SLA). Will link draft after I finish credit calc.

paul: Question for product: do we allow customers to opt into 90-day telemetry for Standard by paying extra? If yes, need a clear price for retention add-on.

ravi: Yes, retention add-on OK. I'll add a retention line item to the spreadsheet.

liz: Docs deliverable: quickstart + streaming example + rate-limit FAQ + error-code table. ETA: 2024-07-02 COB if eng provides demo by 2024-06-27.

mika: Support deliverable: training deck + triage playbook + canned responses. ETA: 2024-07-03 COB.

paul: Canary + rollout policy doc + rollback runbook. ETA: 2024-06-30 EOD.

ravi: Pricing and SLA credit calc spreadsheet. ETA: 2024-06-28 EOD.

anya: I'll convert these into tickets. Final items: ensure each ticket has an acceptance criterion (e.g., SLA doc includes examples of credit calc, docs include sample code that runs end-to-end, support deck includes escalation slides). If nobody objects, I'll create tickets with the above owners/deadlines in 1 hour.

liz: No objections. Minor ask: include a note in docs about streaming p95 expectations being higher — I'll mirror the SLA numbers once theyre finalized.

mika: Also add a short incident communication template for customers (SMS/email) to the runbook.

anya: Will do. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
